# Lessons

## B-dryrun-flake

### upgrade-dry-run flake (B-dryrun-flake): closed unreproduced; read the diagnostics file first on a recurrence

**Rule.** If scripts/ci/upgrade-dry-run fails again, run 'ddflow bug reopen B-dryrun-flake', attach .ddflow/local/dryrun/<stamp>-<run>.json, and read the failing step before changing anything.

**Why.** Closed UNREPRODUCED by operator decision 2026-10-12 (not a false finding, not a fix). It failed 2 of 2 times unexplained (--installed-version 0.2.1 --simulate-old 0.2.1; --build-old) while other agents' suites ran, green on rerun. The one captured failure (1 of 15 loaded runs, --build-old) was step 6 'the handshake did not propose the upgrade' with step 10 PASS, so not a live-repo race: the MCP start check is bounded by [upgrade].start_timeout_s=10 s while 'upgrade --plan' on a ~39k-event log takes 7-11 s, so the check very probably timed out under load (reply text was cut by the transcript bound: inferred, not read). Later: 15/15 and 6 more runs under CPU burners, all green, no diagnostics file; research R99deddaafe (THEORETICAL). Related fixed bugs: B-start-timeout-drops-proposal, B-upgrade-proposal-announced-once.

**How to apply.** Diagnostics already shipped: a failed or could-not-run dry run writes its step table, each command's bounded stdout/stderr and the MCP replies to .ddflow/local/dryrun/ (path printed; --diag-dir / DDFLOW_DRYRUN_DIAG_DIR); rehearsal MCP sessions get 120 s and a timeout is 'unavailable', never pass; step 1 clones committed state at the pinned commit with one retry; step 10 reads each shard once with stat-before/after retry. Step 6 plus a start-check timeout: look at upgrade_start._bounded and upgrade_plan.build cost. 'live repo changed during rehearsal': a shard rewrite by another agent. The closing bar that was not met: 20 consecutive green runs of the 3 variants, at least half under CPU load, plus a clean week of CI.

**Seen in:** B-dryrun-flake

## agents

### Telling agents 'never run the whole suite' also makes them skip the selected ci gate unless the brief names the allowed gate

**Rule.** An agent reads a prohibition literally and over-applies it.

**Why.** Five items merged with ci and bug_hunt recorded unavailable because the brief said no whole-suite runs; `ddflow tests` also prints the full-suite command, which two other agents then ran (13k tests, 20+ minutes).

**How to apply.** Say both halves: the selected-scope `gate run ITEM ci` is required before merge; only a manual whole-suite pytest is forbidden. Brief text now carries this.

**Seen in:** coordinator 2026-10-17

### A background wait loop must end by itself: a deadline, a liveness check, and stopped before the agent reports

**Rule.** Every background 'wait until done' loop has (1) a deadline (e.g. SECONDS-based, exit non-zero when hit), (2) a condition that fails when the watched process DIES, not only a marker the process writes on a clean exit (check the PID with kill -0, or pair the marker test with it), (3) no 'pgrep -f <text>' whose text is in the loop's own command line, and (4) is stopped (TaskStop / kill) before the agent hands back.

**Why.** 2026-09-30: six polling loops ran 5-21 hours after their agents had finished: they waited for EXIT=/FINISHED lines that reviews never wrote because the reviews hung (LAN Qwen), were cancelled, or had their output file overwritten in a shared scratchpad; one 'while pgrep -f "B-fix-declared-family-refute"' matched its own shell and could never end. They cost little CPU but made the task panel show phantom running work for a day.

**How to apply.** Template: pid=$!; end=$((SECONDS+3600)); while kill -0 $pid 2>/dev/null && [ $SECONDS -lt $end ]; do sleep 30; done. Keep output files in a per-agent scratch subfolder. Before reporting, list your background shells and stop any still running.

**Seen in:** B-fix-companions-stale, B-fix-dup-work-deps, B-fix-declared-family

## api

### An api function behind an MCP tool's payload key must carry that key on every path, refusals included

**Rule.** When an api function's Outcome backs an MCP tool with `"payload": "<key>"`, build the projected data (including `<key>`, typically `rows`) BEFORE any validation, and pass it (`**data`) to every `O.refused`/`O.nothing` return as well as the success return. Never return a bare `O.refused(kind, reason)` from such a function. Verify it by calling the tool over MCP with an argument that triggers the refusal and asserting the reason survives -- a CLI test cannot catch this, because the CLI prints `out.reason` without projecting.

**Why.** In `mcp.py`, `_outcome_result` computes `out.body(payload_key)` before its refusal handling, and `Outcome.body(key)` is `self.data[key]`. So a refusal that omits the key raises KeyError, `serve` catches it, and the caller gets JSON-RPC -32603 "internal error: '<key>'" with the real remedy discarded. The CLI half is unaffected, so only an MCP-level test sees it.

**How to apply.** For any new/changed api function with a payload-keyed tool: (1) initialise the data dict with the key before validating; (2) grep the function for `O.refused(`/`O.nothing(` and confirm each passes `**data`; (3) add an MCP test that triggers each refusal and asserts a distinctive reason substring appears (not just a word that also appears in the JSON body).

**Seen in:** B196

## architecture

### A new module of helpers for later consumers needs [kept] entries in unreferenced_functions.toml

**Rule.** Every public helper with no production caller yet is listed under [kept] with the consumer task id, in the same change

**Why.** tests/test_architecture_guards.py ratchet unreferenced_functions has baseline 0; the selected unit_tests run failed on 5 new drift.py helpers

## attribution

### Never keep your ddflow identity in a file another agent can rewrite: pass --agent on the command line itself

**Rule.** Spell --agent <id> (or DDFLOW_AGENT) inline on every ddflow call; do not rely on a wrapper script in a scratch directory.

**Why.** Subagents of one session share its scratchpad. On B-fix-trailer-names-item a wrapper 'dd' holding --agent fix-trailer-id was overwritten by the fix-staged-paths agent with its own id, and 138 events (claim, every gate, merge, complete, bug fixed) were recorded as fix-staged-paths, in that agent's shard.

**How to apply.** Before closing, grep the uncommitted shards for your item id; git status must show your own shard modified.

**Seen in:** B-fix-trailer-names-item

## baseline

### A baseline test run must use a tree nobody is editing

**Rule.** Take the 'before' suite run in a separate detached worktree of the base, never in the worktree you are about to change.

**Why.** On the run_nemo_run cutover a 13-minute baseline ran in the cutover worktree while the rulebooks were being edited; doc-reading tests picked up the edits mid-run and the baseline reported failures the base does not have (67 vs 57 on a clean run).

**How to apply.** git worktree add --detach <path> <base>; run the baseline there; diff failure sets by node id.

## bisect

### When tests fail after a deliberate behaviour change, bisect to the commit and update the TEST; fixing the code reverts the change

**Rule.** Four red-main fixes in a day were stale tests: the lease grace wording, implement-must-be-ahead, phase_full_suite default require.

**Why.** Reading the commit that changed behaviour (git log -S) told the agents which side was wrong in minutes.

**How to apply.** git log -S on the asserted text, read the commit message and decision, then change the test with the reason.

**Seen in:** coordinator 2026-10-17

### A budget turned report-only must be relaxed in every enforcing site

## bug

### Pin every definition of a rule in one table before unifying them

**Rule.** Before routing duplicated predicates through one function, write a test that evaluates every site over the full input grid.

**Seen in:** Bf72f9fb741

### Decide how to launch an installed package from its install provenance (PEP 610 direct_url.json), not from whether a runner like uvx is on PATH

**Rule.** When writing a launch line for an installed Python package, `uvx <name>` (or any index-resolving runner) is only the same program when the running install came from that index. Read the distribution's direct_url.json (PEP 610; present for VCS, local-directory, archive-URL and editable installs, absent for index installs) in the directory that holds the package, and for a non-index install name the installation itself by absolute path (its console script beside sys.executable, else the interpreter with -m). The presence of uvx on PATH says nothing about where the package lives.

**Seen in:** B8ff258154d

### A hand-built TOML writer must parse its own output before replacing the file

**Rule.** json.dumps is valid TOML only for strings, numbers and arrays of them; a dict becomes JSON, which TOML rejects. Any writer that assembles TOML by string formatting must render tables as TOML inline tables and parse the merged result (tomllib.loads) before the atomic write, so a malformed block is refused instead of leaving a config no later command can load.

**Seen in:** B-reviewers-add-launch-json

### A fold's 'what the item still knows' must include every claim, not just the ones a branch happened to keep

**Rule.** When a fold decides overlaps from remembered state, every path that replaces, renews or caps that state must keep the old claim reachable: a branch that just overwrites (same-holder re-claim), a cap that drops the oldest, or a lookup that searches one list of two each silently hides a real conflict. Write the invariant as a property over random histories with every event kind interleaved in every per-writer-consistent order, and run it against the unfixed code first.

**Seen in:** Bee8e21c547

### A set-valued lookup must union every match, not stop at the first

**Rule.** When a substring map returns a SET that a safety check compares against, take the union of every matching key (and treat any empty match as unknown); first-match-wins on key order under-approximates the set and turns into a false pass.

**Seen in:** B15af2d6420

### A check that watches the working tree cannot run where other processes write it

**Rule.** In a ddflow checkout, agents append to committed .ddflow/events/*.jsonl continuously, so any tool that diffs the working tree before and after a step (pre-commit's 'files were modified by this hook', a formatter's --check on the whole tree, a 'git status is clean' assertion) fails there at random, and the longer the step the likelier. Run such checks in a scratch worktree of the commit under test (git worktree add --detach), which has no other writers and also tests the commit rather than uncommitted state.

**Seen in:** B431fff0197

### A git hook's reads must not depend on which GIT_* variables the runner kept: run them in the committing tree

**Rule.** Commit-hook git reads run in the tree being committed (the hook's cwd toplevel, if it belongs to this repository), inheriting GIT_INDEX_FILE; never git -C <primary>. When simulating a hook, set every variable git exports: a linked worktree's hook gets GIT_DIR as well as GIT_INDEX_FILE, and GIT_DIR alone had been masking this bug in real commits.

**Seen in:** Bba366d9893

### An import that may change existing items must read provenance from the log, not the fold

**Rule.** When a re-run of an importer may complete or alter an item already in the queue, decide 'untouched since import' from the event log (every event on the subject was the importer's own), and decide a child's done-ness by who set its CURRENT state. The folded state cannot tell open-because-untouched from open-because-reopened. Also run 'python -m ddflow' from a neutral cwd when testing a worktree: -m puts cwd first on sys.path, so running from the primary checkout silently uses main's code.

**Seen in:** B45d5aa72fa

### A doctor finding about parallel work must consult the dependency graph readiness uses

**Rule.** Before warning that items 'cannot run in parallel', check whether inherited_deps (plus a dependency covering its descendants) already orders them; and when narrowing a group, apply the size threshold to the group, never to the narrowed subset.

**Seen in:** Bd1c601896f

### A free-form 'source' field is prose until proven a path: parse it as one token or not at all, and never let a stat crash a report

**Rule.** When a check stats paths taken from a human-written field (seen_in, sources), accept only one whitespace- and markup-free token (a whole markdown link as its target), count the rest in a note, and stat with os.stat so only ENOENT/ENOTDIR mean vanished -- Path.is_file raises on ENAMETOOLONG on 3.11-3.13 and returns False on 3.14.

**Seen in:** Bd5b59f3894

### A hook counts as armed only if the thing that runs it would run ddflow's check on every commit

**Rule.** When detecting another tool's hook (pre-commit framework), model its skip rules -- stages/default_stages, file filters without always_run, pass_filenames, language fail/pygrep, remote manifests -- and report anything unreadable or unverifiable as NOT installed with the reason; three reviewers each found a false 'installed' the first version missed.

**Seen in:** B259fd32dbd

### A 'last line is the max' shortcut only holds while a file has exactly one writer; merge=union silently gives it two

**Rule.** Any O(1) summary read from an append-only file's tail (clock, counter, high-water mark) is valid only under a single-writer invariant. If the file is ever combined by merge=union, sync, or copy from another clone, that invariant is gone and nothing on disk records it: derive the summary from the whole (cached) content, and make identities that name a writer unique per clone, not just per host and directory.

**Seen in:** B28589b8b26

### Never let 0 (or "") mean both 'unset' and a real value: use None for unset

**Rule.** When a numeric or string option has a default, represent 'not given' as None on every surface (argparse default=None, MCP a.get(k) is None) and validate the explicit value; `x or DEFAULT` silently turns an explicit 0/'' into the default, and in a safety tool that flips the answer in the unsafe direction.

**Seen in:** B22-minzero

## bugs

### Close a bug found mid-task with 'bug fixed' BEFORE merging the item

**Rule.** Run ddflow bug fixed <id> --regression-test ... while the item's worktree still exists; after merge the worktree is gone and the regression check records could-not-run

**Why.** bug fixed verifies the regression test against the pre-fix source from the fix task's worktree; merge removes it (B4dd9658753, Bd5adf89e33 both closed could-not-run; both were verified by hand against main's code)

## chunking

### A review finding that a new file is empty is the chunker, not the diff

**Rule.** When ddflow review reports a newly added file as empty or hunk-less, check the file exists with content and treat the finding as the split_diff header-only-chunk artefact (bug B-split-diff-header-chunk) until that is fixed.

**Why.** Three DeepSeek reviews of B-fix-gate-config-drift each raised a HIGH 'tests/test_gate_config_drift.py is empty' finding; split_diff sends the file header alone in one chunk when the file exceeds the budget.

**Seen in:** B-fix-gate-config-drift

## ci

### Run ruff format (and ruff check) on the Python files you touched before every commit

**Rule.** Before committing or running the item's gates, run 'uv run ruff format <touched files>' and 'uv run ruff check <touched files>'; put pure formatting changes in their own commit. Agents must not leave formatting to the pre-push hook or to CI.

**Why.** On 2026-10-24..26 the CI Lint step and the pre-push stage failed repeatedly on 'ruff format --check' and 'ruff check' (an unused variable in a test, unformatted files after merges), found only at push time or by an unlucky agent's ci; each cost a red main, a bug, and an agent run. ruff format is deterministic and takes under a second.

**How to apply.** In a worktree: 'uv run ruff format <files> && uv run ruff check <files>' before 'git commit'; for a merge conflict resolution re-run it on the merged files; when fixing a Bci-ruff-* bug run 'uv run ruff format .' only on the failing files and commit it separately with a short message; 'ddflow precommit' runs the project's hooks if you want the exact CI set.

**Seen in:** Bci-ruff-format-check-ci-lint-71de8acaec-8d0f618, Bci-ruff-check-ci-lint-28f149cf83-12d29f5, B3943adc584

### Python 3.12.3 argparse breaks '--' for pytest: never rely on it to protect a dash-led argument

**Rule.** Do not use '--' to make a user-supplied value safe from an option parser: check it yourself and ./-prefix it. A test green on dev Python (3.12.13/3.13) can fail on the runner's 3.12.3.

**Why.** CI publish verify failed: 'pytest -- --co' ran collect-only (exit 5) on 3.12.3, exit 4 'not found' elsewhere.

### A hook-line change merged with tests/test_compaction_summary.py still asserting the old line

**Rule.** When a generated command line changes, grep tests for the old literal, not only the selector's reach

**Why.** B-hx-migrate's selected scope did not reach test_compaction_summary; main went red and the next item's full ci found it

**How to apply.** grep -rn the old line text under tests/ before ci

### A worker count fixed in a committed hook (-n auto) is per-core on the host that runs it

**Rule.** Substitute the computed count in the local runner (a temp copy of the hook config), keep the committed config for CI, and bound concurrent full runs host-wide

**Why.** B26b5951f2b: 2-3 CI-parity runs of 192 workers each gave load 337

### A change to ddflow/api makes ddflow tests and the ci gate the whole suite (about 16 minutes)

**Rule.** Prefer putting new logic in a module no hub imports; budget a full ci run when ddflow.api changes; use gate run ci --rerun-failed after a fix

**Why.** B-hx-cli: ddflow tests said WHOLE SUITE (221 importing files) while still listing a selection

**How to apply.** ddflow gate run ITEM ci --rerun-failed

### A pinned transcript must not hold what varies by Python version or by machine

**Rule.** Normalise argparse layout (usage wrapping, choice quoting) on both sides of a pin through tests/pin_norm.stable, and fix OS user, host name and PATH tools in the harness; never record them from the developer's box.

**Why.** Seven tests passed for months on the developer's Python 3.13 and machine, then failed together on a CI runner (3.12.3, user runner, no pre-commit): wrapped usage lines, quoted choices, getpass user, hostname-prefixed shard names, and precommit's installed/found booleans were all pinned verbatim.

**How to apply.** Reproduce before fixing: a sitecustomize that patches socket.gethostname, getpass.getuser and PATH, run on /usr/bin/python3.12. Prove a normaliser keeps its power by mutating a pinned word. A stdlib bug (3.12.3 communicate resume) needs a cause-level test that fails on every Python, since the behavioural one only fails on the buggy interpreter.

### A gate that checks a committed ref cannot be proved by a working-tree mutation

**Rule.** Before registering a mutation for a gate, check what the gate reads: gate verify edits the worktree uncommitted, so a gate that checks HEAD (ci) reports PASSED on mutated source and the proof is vacuous in the wrong direction.

**Why.** gate verify <item> ci ran 19.5 min / 1264 cpu-min and said ci cannot see the mutation; ci run merges the committed branch in a scratch tree (B-verify-ci-blind). A related trap: a test that asserts a registered mutation applies exactly once turns the gate red for EVERY mutation, because the suite runs with the mutation applied (the critic caught it).

**How to apply.** Register mutations only for gates that read the working tree (unit_tests). For a committed-ref gate, fix verify to commit the mutation first. Keep any test about the registry tolerant of the applied state.

**Seen in:** U4-mutation-registry

### A change to the default pipelines must run the slow scenarios before it lands

**Rule.** When a default gate, pipeline or completion rule changes, run 'pytest tests/test_scenarios.py -m slow' before merging: the unit_tests gate runs addopts' 'not slow', so the scenarios that drive a phase to completion never see the change, and CI is the first place they run.

**Why.** 8aa8170 added the phase 'docs' gate; every local gate passed, and main went red in CI because two scenarios closed P1 without it (bug B6d601e6ba0).

**How to apply.** The pre-push hook (.pre-commit-config.yaml, 'pre-commit install') now runs the scenarios whenever ddflow/, demos/ or tests/ changed; do not SKIP=scenarios on a push that touches gates, pipelines or complete.

**Seen in:** B-fix-ci-red

## claims

### ddflow update --globs REPLACES the whole glob list: pass every glob you still need

**Rule.** To add a glob, restate the full list with the addition

**Why.** update --globs sets the list; it does not append, so an omitted glob is silently dropped from the claim and from overlap checks, leaving files unprotected

**How to apply.** ddflow show <id> to read the current globs, then update --globs with old plus new, and show again to confirm

**Seen in:** P-unify

## cli

### Read a subcommand's help before its flags when the verb was not used today

**Rule.** Any ddflow subcommand not run in this session yet: run  before passing flags not seen this session.

**How to apply.** hard blocker: ensuring guesses cost more than helps.

### A new top-level CLI command needs a covered-by declaration or tests/test_mcp_parity.py fails only in ci

**Rule.** When adding a CLI verb that rides an existing MCP tool as an action, also add Command(path=(verb,), reason=...) in surfaces/declared

**Why.** B-hx-cli: harness list/show/doctor passed the item's own tests and the 1837-test selection, and failed test_every_cli_command_is_reachable_over_mcp after a 16 minute whole-suite ci

**How to apply.** Run tests/test_mcp_parity.py tests/test_command_registry.py right after adding a parser

## complete

### A task split with `ddflow split` closes when its children are done: do not try to complete the parent

**Rule.** The parent's own gates stay empty by design.

**Why.** fleet-trunk3 stopped on a refused `ddflow complete SE-kind-data` that was already done.

**How to apply.** After the last child completes, `ddflow show PARENT` instead of completing it.

**Seen in:** coordinator 2026-10-17

## concurrency

### A test double that counts a request in flight until AFTER it writes the response measures the socket, not the work

**Rule.** Release a request counter when the work it represents ends, BEFORE writing the response; assert concurrency by that mechanism (the count during the work), never by a wall-clock ratio. A counter kept until after wfile.write/response-send is descheduled under load, so a strictly sequential client reads its count as 2.

**Why.** fix-B32e97ebbb8: _Fake released in_flight in a finally AFTER wfile.write; a client starts the next sequential chunk the instant it reads the previous response, so when the server thread was descheduled the next request overlapped the not-yet-decremented one and a max_concurrency=1 run read peak==2 -- the concurrency test then flaked only under the end-to-end scenario load. Reproduced 1/40 sequential runs under load before, 0/40 after.

**How to apply.** In a fake server, decrement the in-flight counter right after simulating the work (the delay), before send_response/wfile.write, with a one-shot flag so the finally is only a safety net. peak is then deterministic (1 sequential, N concurrent). Prefer this to a timing ratio (t_par < t_seq/2), which distorts under load.

**Seen in:** fix-B32e97ebbb8

## config

### ddflow copies .roborev.toml into each worktree at creation: changing the primary's reviewer pin leaves older worktrees on the old model

**Rule.** After changing .roborev.toml (model, backup) or a served model name, update the copies in existing worktrees (.ddflow/worktrees/*/.roborev.toml), then check a fresh job's model in 'roborev list --json'.

**Why.** 2026-10-19: the LAN Flash host renamed its model (…-Flash-1017); worktrees created earlier still pinned the old name, so roborev job 3107 failed with ProviderModelNotFoundError and standards went unavailable. Fixed 5 stale copies by hand.

**How to apply.** Bug Bbc4f952ca9 tracks the root cause; the fix is to resolve the roborev config from the primary at job time, not a frozen copy.

### roborev: a repo .roborev.toml overrides [REDACTED:path]; check a FRESH job's recorded model after changing either

**Rule.** After changing roborev model/agent, enqueue a fresh review and read its model field in 'roborev list --json'; queued jobs keep the model and prompt they were enqueued with.

**Why.** default_model in the global config did nothing because the repo .roborev.toml pins agent/model/backup; the first three test reviews still ran on the Flash host.

**How to apply.** Check the LAN vLLM load first (curl host:8000/metrics, vllm:num_requests_running): a shared Flash host at ~140 concurrent requests made every kilo step ~30 s while Pro idled. 'roborev pause' survives a daemon restart; resume with 'roborev unpause'.

### A config section must land with the code that reads it, or the dead-knob ratchet refuses it

**Rule.** Do not slice a config section into a task of its own when its readers come later: the dead-knob ratchet (tests/test_ratchet_no_dead_knobs.py) requires every documented knob to be read by code, and its allowlist may only shrink, so a section with no reader cannot pass ci. Declare the knobs in the task that first consumes them, or wire a real reader in the same change.

**Why.** A knob an operator can set that nothing consumes is a lie in the documentation, and the repo makes that mechanically detectable -- so the ratchet is working as designed and the SLICE was wrong, not the test.

**How to apply.** Before filing or claiming a "config section" task: grep the planned consumers, and if they are separate items that depend on it, merge the section into the first consumer. Run `uv run pytest tests/test_ratchet_no_dead_knobs.py -q` before committing a new knob.

**Seen in:** B-docs-config

**Rule.** 

## critic

### A reasoning-model reviewer at low temperature loops until its token budget is gone

**Rule.** Run reasoning-model reviewers at the vendor's recommended temperature (DeepSeek: 1.0), not ddflow's 0.3 default; before blaming chunk size or reasoning_effort, read the reasoning tail

**Why.** 2026-09-29: lan-deepseek-v4.1-flash at temperature 0.3 truncated chunk 1 of 223d493 at 64000 reasoning tokens on every reasoning_effort tried (low, high, 25; top-level and chat_template_kwargs); the reasoning tail was 'OK, NO FINDINGS. ... let me reconsider' repeated. At 1.0 the same diff reviewed fully in 419 s. thinking=false finished in 121 s but reported clean where a thinking run found issues.

**How to apply.** Set temperature = 1.0 on the [[reviewer]] in .ddflow/reviewers.toml. To diagnose, wrap services.review._open and dump choices[0].message.reasoning_content's tail.

**Seen in:** recovery session s20260929T151921-3202694

### The roborev daemon leaks a .kilo process per review, which saturates the shared LAN reviewer

**Rule.** Before and during long review work, reap orphaned '.kilo run' processes (ppid 1); run one review at a time per LAN endpoint

**Why.** 2026-09-29: the roborev daemon (roborev daemon run) spawns 'node kilo run' -> '.kilo run' per job; when the job ends the node launcher exits and the native .kilo child is re-parented to init and keeps querying the LAN endpoint. 18 were reaped at one point, 9 more an hour later; with them live every ddflow critic timed out at 3600 s or came back off-contract. Wrapping roborev in 'timeout' leaks the same way.

**How to apply.** for p in $(pgrep -f 'kilo run --format json'); do [ "$(ps -o ppid= -p $p | tr -d ' ')" = 1 ] && kill $p; done -- or restart the roborev daemon; the durable fix belongs in roborev/kilo (kill the process group).

**Seen in:** recovery session s20260929T151921-3202694

## ddflow

### With several agents on one queue, never file under the next free number: use a descriptive id (B-<slug>) and confirm it is unused

**Rule.** Before task add, pick an id derived from the work (B-add-refuses-dup-id), not max(B<n>)+1, and confirm it is free (ddflow show <id> must fail). Parallel agents each guess the same next number from their own view, and an add over an existing id overwrote that item's title/globs without warning, even a claimed one mid-pipeline (a duplicate id is now refused, but a numbered id still races). If a numbered id is required, re-read ddflow status immediately before adding.

**Why.** 2026-09-28: three agents each picked the next number within minutes (B205-B208 collided twice); four other agents' items were overwritten, one claimed and mid-pipeline, and one agent's lease and gate records ended up under another agent's title, where complete would have counted them.

**How to apply.** for id in ...; do ddflow show $id >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo TAKEN; done before filing. After a collision: void the stray gate records with a reason, release, re-file under a new id, remove the duplicates; restore a clobbered item by re-adding its prior task.added fields from the event log.

**Seen in:** B16042585f4, B6bd279367e

## decide

### A task that needs a decide task is stuck for good once the decide task is abandoned as a decision

**Rule.** Do not put a decide task in another task's needs; the decision record governs by globs. If one is there, drop the edge with ddflow update --needs once the decision is recorded.

**Why.** ddflow treats an abandoned prerequisite as unsatisfied and the convention settles a decide task by abandoning it. 67 tasks waited forever on 2026-10-15 (9 on nothing else); the brief said 'X is abandoned' but nothing called it stuck.

**How to apply.** Before abandoning a decide task, list its dependents (ddflow show of the dependents, or the next output) and drop the edge; doctor will report such an edge once B9eeecd134c is fixed.

## decisions

### Check the queue before applying review-proposed edges; operator answers can contradict each other

**Rule.** Before applying a roadmap-review edit list, re-read each task's current needs/globs: five edge fixes were already in the queue, and two same-day accepted decisions (D-config-layer-order vs D-jinja-trust-reaffirmed) disagree on where jinja_extensions lives.

**Why.** Applying stale proposals duplicates work; recording an answer without checking it against sibling decisions creates a new contradiction.

**How to apply.** Diff proposed edges against the snapshot first; when a new decision names operator-only keys, grep the other same-day decisions for those keys.

### Accepting a proposed decision by re-adding it from another identity makes it CONTESTED: pass the proposer's --agent or resolve with --keep

**Rule.** Two definitions from different agents mean none is in force.

**Why.** Happened twice on 2026-10-17 (D-continuous-improvement, five -r2 decisions).

**How to apply.** Use the same --agent as the proposal, or run `ddflow resolve ID --keep <agent>` straight away; DX-decision-accept-cmd will add a status change.

**Seen in:** coordinator 2026-10-17

## declared

### A declared command needs three registrations by convention: declared file, parser by_convention, lifecycle re-export + wire_shape

**Rule.** A new declared family needs help_group, wire_shape, no top-level api import in declared/, and its api function re-exported in api/lifecycle/__init__

**Why.** ddflow sync hit test_declared_commands, test_lifecycle_layout, test_api_layer, test_architecture_guards one after another

## deepseek

### With the refute-not-review reviewer, a round always finds something: batch fixes and stop editing the diff between rounds

**Rule.** Collect all findings from one concurrent rubber_duck+critic round, fix or refute them together, then re-run both once; do not commit between a round's start and its result.

**Why.** B-fix-trailer-names-item took 13 DeepSeek rounds (~30 min each): every edit changed the diff and invited a new marginal finding, and two findings flip-flopped (startswith vs substring for dict types).

**How to apply.** Refute with a probe (e.g. git commit -v, Ctx.repo_root) instead of editing when the finding is false; a chunk that truncates at 64k reasoning tokens makes the gate PARTIAL regardless.

**Seen in:** B-fix-trailer-names-item

**Why.** 2026-09-29: lan-deepseek-v4.1-flash at temperature 0.3 truncated chunk 1 of 223d493 at 64000 reasoning tokens on every reasoning_effort tried (low, high, 25; top-level and chat_template_kwargs); the reasoning tail was 'OK, NO FINDINGS. ... let me reconsider' repeated. At 1.0 the same diff reviewed fully in 419 s. thinking=false finished in 121 s but reported clean where a thinking run found issues.

**How to apply.** Set temperature = 1.0 on the [[reviewer]] in .ddflow/reviewers.toml. To diagnose, wrap services.review._open and dump choices[0].message.reasoning_content's tail.

## delta

### A delta review sees one commit, so a fix landed earlier on the branch reads as 'no fix'

**Rule.** After a follow-up commit on a fix branch, expect the deepseek delta reviewer to report 'the diff does not fix the bug' / 'the test cannot fail'; refute with the earlier commit and its failing-first probe, or run --full so the reviewer sees the whole branch.

**Why.** On fix-B20dc45f4c5, fix-B279a0ebfc1 and fix-B7395b84149 (2026-10-07) every delta round after a small follow-up commit produced HIGH findings claiming the fix was absent; each was false -- the fix was in an earlier commit of the same branch. --context did not prevent it; a --full round reviewed the branch correctly.

**Seen in:** fix-B20dc45f4c5, fix-B279a0ebfc1, fix-B7395b84149

## deps

### A task in a phase must not depend on a task that is already done in the same phase, nor on itself, to express ordering

**Rule.** Declare deps only on open work outside a cycle; a done dependency is noise and a self or phase-sibling cycle blocks the item

**Why.** phase-level deps count a phase's open tasks, so a task depending on its own phase (or on an item that closes only with that phase) is blocked by itself: brief shows 'phase has 1 open task(s)' forever

**How to apply.** When filing, check ddflow show <id> deps; a follow-up that must wait for the phase belongs in a later phase, not a dependency on its own phase

**Seen in:** P-unify

## diagnostics

### Unexplained failure with no repro: ship diagnostics first, then fix what they show

**Rule.** When a check failed twice, passed on rerun and cannot be reproduced, do not guess a cause: first make the next failure explain itself (persist the failing step's table and each command's bounded stdout/stderr to a git-ignored file whose path is printed in the failure line), harden only what you can show misjudges, then run it repeatedly under load.

**Why.** B-dryrun-flake: the two failures of scripts/ci/upgrade-dry-run left nothing; 15 reruns passed, and the three suspected causes (clone racing git writes, live shards read mid-write, another agent's snapshot tag counted as ours) were real misjudgements in unit tests but are not what the first captured failure was. That one (1 in 15 loaded runs) was step 6: the MCP handshake did not propose the upgrade. The server's start check is bounded by [upgrade].start_timeout_s (10 s), the plan of this repository's 39k-event log takes 7-11 s, so under load it very probably timed out; the transcript cut the reply text (a command that exits 0 keeps few characters), so this is inferred, not read.

**How to apply.** Add the transcript before the fix; keep the reply a step judges (not only the exit code) in it; make load-dependent product bounds explicit in the rehearsal (give it time, and report a timeout as unavailable, never pass or fail). Close the bug only on 20 green loaded runs plus a clean week.

**Seen in:** B-dryrun-flake

## docs

### Read vendor docs as raw sources: summarising fetches hid Copilot's cost model change and Antigravity's wrapping ban

**Rule.** For per-agent facts use curl on raw markdown/HTML (github/docs, vscode-docs, product docs) and grep the text; check the billing page's date before trusting a cost lever

**Why.** Pass 1 listed premium-request multipliers as Copilot's lever and Antigravity as unresearched; raw pages showed per-token AI Credits since 2026-06-01 and an FAQ forbidding agy inside other agents on consumer plans

**How to apply.** curl --compressed + a tag stripper under python3 -I into a scratch dir; GitHub trees API lists doc paths; quote exact setting names with file and date

**Seen in:** ATF-research-pass2

## docsync

### git grep -o undercounts with many -F patterns: re-match whole lines instead

**Rule.** To learn WHICH of many fixed-string patterns occur, run git grep without -o and re-match the returned lines in Python

**Why.** B17 research: git grep --cached -o -h -w -F with ~190 -e patterns reported agent_id 19 times while -c showed it in many files, so live identifiers looked deleted

**How to apply.** git grep -h -w -F -e ... (whole lines), then set(regex.findall(lines))

**Seen in:** B17

## doctor

### a sticky 'lost events' flag set by one look at a shard mid-rewrite

**Rule.** when a detector's flag is sticky, a single unlocked read of a file another process rewrites in place must be re-looked until it stops changing before it flags

**Why.** shard-marks flagged coordinator/fleet-dx-o/fleet-unblock-e as lost though the last seen event was still at line 3144 of 3860; the flag only clears on byte-exact size

**How to apply.** shardmarks._settled outside the marks lock; compare the mark to the file with the event in it before believing the doctor

## enforce

### A new pre-commit check must be run against the repo's own generated files

**Rule.** Before enforcing a digest/marker check on staged files, run it over this repo's real README and docs

**Why.** region_check shared the ddflow:begin grammar with the README views but the two digest the body differently; the check would have refused every README commit (caught only by roborev standards)

**How to apply.** Add a test built on every writer of the grammar (render_region and readme_region), and run the check on the repo's own files

### Three ddflow:begin marker grammars coexist

**Rule.** A check over ddflow:begin/end markers must know all three: doc/name sha= (regions.py), legacy doc=X body-sha256=, and adopt's NAME ddflow=V fmt=N sha= (pins/adopt)

**Why.** The pre-commit region check treated adopt's stamped end markers in CLAUDE.md as unbalanced; the ci gate caught it in test_driver_drift

**How to apply.** Run the check against the repo's own CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md before shipping

## fake

### A test double that counts a request in flight until AFTER it writes the response measures the socket, not the work

**Rule.** Release a request counter when the work it represents ends, BEFORE writing the response; assert concurrency by that mechanism (the count during the work), never by a wall-clock ratio. A counter kept until after wfile.write/response-send is descheduled under load, so a strictly sequential client reads its count as 2.

**Why.** fix-B32e97ebbb8: _Fake released in_flight in a finally AFTER wfile.write; a client starts the next sequential chunk the instant it reads the previous response, so when the server thread was descheduled the next request overlapped the not-yet-decremented one and a max_concurrency=1 run read peak==2 -- the concurrency test then flaked only under the end-to-end scenario load. Reproduced 1/40 sequential runs under load before, 0/40 after.

**How to apply.** In a fake server, decrement the in-flight counter right after simulating the work (the delay), before send_response/wfile.write, with a one-shot flag so the finally is only a safety net. peak is then deterministic (1 sequential, N concurrent). Prefer this to a timing ratio (t_par < t_seq/2), which distorts under load.

**Seen in:** fix-B32e97ebbb8

## flake

### upgrade-dry-run flake (B-dryrun-flake): closed unreproduced; read the diagnostics file first on a recurrence

**Rule.** If scripts/ci/upgrade-dry-run fails again, run 'ddflow bug reopen B-dryrun-flake', attach .ddflow/local/dryrun/<stamp>-<run>.json, and read the failing step before changing anything.

**Why.** Closed UNREPRODUCED by operator decision 2026-10-12 (not a false finding, not a fix). It failed 2 of 2 times unexplained (--installed-version 0.2.1 --simulate-old 0.2.1; --build-old) while other agents' suites ran, green on rerun. The one captured failure (1 of 15 loaded runs, --build-old) was step 6 'the handshake did not propose the upgrade' with step 10 PASS, so not a live-repo race: the MCP start check is bounded by [upgrade].start_timeout_s=10 s while 'upgrade --plan' on a ~39k-event log takes 7-11 s, so the check very probably timed out under load (reply text was cut by the transcript bound: inferred, not read). Later: 15/15 and 6 more runs under CPU burners, all green, no diagnostics file; research R99deddaafe (THEORETICAL). Related fixed bugs: B-start-timeout-drops-proposal, B-upgrade-proposal-announced-once.

**How to apply.** Diagnostics already shipped: a failed or could-not-run dry run writes its step table, each command's bounded stdout/stderr and the MCP replies to .ddflow/local/dryrun/ (path printed; --diag-dir / DDFLOW_DRYRUN_DIAG_DIR); rehearsal MCP sessions get 120 s and a timeout is 'unavailable', never pass; step 1 clones committed state at the pinned commit with one retry; step 10 reads each shard once with stat-before/after retry. Step 6 plus a start-check timeout: look at upgrade_start._bounded and upgrade_plan.build cost. 'live repo changed during rehearsal': a shard rewrite by another agent. The closing bar that was not met: 20 consecutive green runs of the 3 variants, at least half under CPU load, plus a clean week of CI.

**Seen in:** B-dryrun-flake

## gates

### Check gate status before ddflow merge; chained commands skip the check

**Rule.** Run ddflow gate status and read every box before merge; never chain gate run, record, merge and complete in one command

**Why.** DX-agent-final-summary merged with ci and unit_tests unrecorded and left main red (B94d11818c1)

### Gates are superseded by any new commit; do all fixes and merge main before starting ci and unit_tests

**Rule.** Finish review fixes, merge main and regenerate pins, then run ci and unit_tests once

**Why.** each run took 10+ minutes and was discarded when the head moved

### A partial baseline-red ci makes unit_tests run the whole suite

**Rule.** when ci is partial baseline-red, the unit_tests gate escalates to the full suite; stop and ask rather than run it

**Why.** scope: the ci gate is partial, the whole suite has not passed on this tree (seen on DX-tests-cmd-not-full-suite)

### A change to ddflow/api/gates.py or services/gates/* must run test_layering, test_module_splits and test_gate_econ_tests before merge

**Rule.** Those files sit at an import cycle and a 600-line module limit.

**Why.** Three merges to the gates code broke main in one day (module size, an api<->api.gates cycle, a ruff import order).

**How to apply.** Add those three test files to the item's selected tests by hand when the diff touches the gates code.

**Seen in:** coordinator 2026-10-17

### A gate that checks a committed ref cannot be proved by a working-tree mutation

**Rule.** Before registering a mutation for a gate, check what the gate reads: gate verify edits the worktree uncommitted, so a gate that checks HEAD (ci) reports PASSED on mutated source and the proof is vacuous in the wrong direction.

**Why.** gate verify <item> ci ran 19.5 min / 1264 cpu-min and said ci cannot see the mutation; ci run merges the committed branch in a scratch tree (B-verify-ci-blind). A related trap: a test that asserts a registered mutation applies exactly once turns the gate red for EVERY mutation, because the suite runs with the mutation applied (the critic caught it).

**How to apply.** Register mutations only for gates that read the working tree (unit_tests). For a committed-ref gate, fix verify to commit the mutation first. Keep any test about the registry tolerant of the applied state.

**Seen in:** U4-mutation-registry

### An unreviewed review chunk is not a full pass: re-run it before recording the gate passed

**Rule.** If a review chunk comes back off-contract or unreviewed, re-run only that chunk (ddflow review <id> --gate G --chunk N) before recording the gate passed; if it still fails, record the gate partial or unavailable with the chunk named.

**Why.** U4 recorded both review gates passed on B-uni-hooks.2-mcpconfig with chunk 7 of 8 unreviewed (2026-10-07); a partly reviewed diff is a coverage gap, not a pass.

**How to apply.** Use --chunk N for the failed chunk; the result merges into the recorded review. Name the chunk in the gate evidence when it cannot be reviewed.

### Confirm an enabled different-family reviewer exists before the critic gates, not at completion

**Rule.** Before starting the critic/rubber_duck gates, run `ddflow reviewers list` and confirm there is an ENABLED reviewer whose family differs from the author's. A reviewer with `gates = []` is disabled; roborev (or any same-family reviewer) does not satisfy the independence check even when it reviews the diff, and `ddflow complete` refuses on it with "--force overrides". If no different-family reviewer is enabled, ask the operator up front whether to enable one or to accept the coverage gap, rather than discovering it at completion time.

**Why.** On B-dupes-sweep the only enabled reviewer (lan-deepseek-v4.1-flash) was the author's own family, and the alibaba Qwen was disabled by the operator's local config (gates = []). Three roborev rounds and a full suite were run before `complete` refused on independence, forcing a `--force` the operator had to authorize mid-task.

**Seen in:** B-dupes-sweep

### A change to the default pipelines must run the slow scenarios before it lands

**Rule.** When a default gate, pipeline or completion rule changes, run 'pytest tests/test_scenarios.py -m slow' before merging: the unit_tests gate runs addopts' 'not slow', so the scenarios that drive a phase to completion never see the change, and CI is the first place they run.

**Why.** 8aa8170 added the phase 'docs' gate; every local gate passed, and main went red in CI because two scenarios closed P1 without it (bug B6d601e6ba0).

**How to apply.** The pre-push hook (.pre-commit-config.yaml, 'pre-commit install') now runs the scenarios whenever ddflow/, demos/ or tests/ changed; do not SKIP=scenarios on a push that touches gates, pipelines or complete.

**Seen in:** B-fix-ci-red

### A gate command is read from the primary checkout but runs with the item branch's dependencies: merge main before unit_tests after the gate config changes

**Rule.** Before running the unit_tests gate, merge the base branch into the item branch whenever main changed .ddflow/config.toml's gate commands or the dev dependencies (e.g. the pytest-xdist '-n 48' change, 8fe68e6).

**Why.** load_gates reads the primary .ddflow/config.toml, but the command executes in the item's worktree with that branch's pyproject.toml/uv.lock; a branch cut before pytest-xdist was added fails with 'unrecognized arguments: -n 48'.

**How to apply.** git merge main in the item worktree (uv run then syncs the new dev deps), rerun the gate.

**Seen in:** B-parallel-tests

## git

### Never git stash in a worktree: the stash stack is shared by every worktree and agent

**Rule.** Set work aside with a WIP commit, never git stash or stash pop

**Why.** refs/stash is one stack for the primary checkout and all linked worktrees; another lane's pop applies or drops your entry (or you take theirs)

**How to apply.** Use a temporary WIP commit; if a stash is unavoidable use stash push -u -m with a unique tag, capture its SHA, restore with stash apply SHA, drop by re-finding the tag

**Seen in:** P-unify

### Mutation-test a file from a saved copy, never undo the mutant with git checkout while the file has uncommitted edits

**Rule.** Before mutating a file to prove a test fails, commit the real edit or cp the file aside; restore with cp from that copy

**Why.** B-fix-registry-504: 'git checkout <file>' to drop a one-line mutant also discarded the uncommitted review fix in the same file; caught only because git diff --stat showed the file missing

**How to apply.** cp f /scratch/f.bak; sed mutant; run test; cp /scratch/f.bak f; git diff --stat

**Seen in:** B-fix-registry-504

### git grep -o undercounts with many -F patterns: re-match whole lines instead

**Rule.** To learn WHICH of many fixed-string patterns occur, run git grep without -o and re-match the returned lines in Python

**Why.** B17 research: git grep --cached -o -h -w -F with ~190 -e patterns reported agent_id 19 times while -c showed it in many files, so live identifiers looked deleted

**How to apply.** git grep -h -w -F -e ... (whole lines), then set(regex.findall(lines))

**Seen in:** B17

## globs

### ddflow's glob overlap check is conservative about *: a * in a directory position overlaps almost everything

**Rule.** Write task globs as literal paths or literal-directory patterns; never put * in a directory position

**Why.** Spot-checked 2026-10-10 on core.globs: match('a/*.py','a/b/c.py') is False, so a single * does NOT cross a slash when matching a path. But overlap() -- the check the scheduler and the lease system use -- treats a * as able to span a slash: overlap('a/*/x.toml','a/y.toml') and overlap('a/*.py','a/b/c.py') are both True. A task glob like tests/guard_baselines/*/ddflow.api.lifecycle.*.toml therefore looked as if it overlapped every baseline file, and only one of 20 cleanup tasks was offered while five lanes waited about 20 minutes each and stopped.

**How to apply.** Before filing a phase, expand the globs against the tree and run core.globs.overlap pairwise on tasks that can run together; replace dir-position wildcards with explicit directories (as was done for P-unify-cleanup).

### A wildcard task glob makes the scheduler treat the task as overlapping every sibling under its prefix

**Rule.** Declare literal file paths on tasks meant to run in parallel; reserve ** for tasks that really own the tree

**Why.** overlap is prefix-based, so ddflow/** or a broad dir/* serialises or refuses lanes whose real files are disjoint, and a claim refused for it cannot be fixed by waiting

**How to apply.** Narrow task globs to the exact files at filing time; at claim time use literal --globs, then widen with update once the holder finishes (restating the full list)

**Seen in:** P-unify

### ddflow update --globs REPLACES the whole glob list: pass every glob you still need

**Rule.** To add a glob, restate the full list with the addition

**Why.** update --globs sets the list; it does not append, so an omitted glob is silently dropped from the claim and from overlap checks, leaving files unprotected

**How to apply.** ddflow show <id> to read the current globs, then update --globs with old plus new, and show again to confirm

**Seen in:** P-unify

### A '**' glob conflicts with every live claim under its literal prefix: claim literal paths when a sibling holds a file in the same directory

**Rule.** globs_overlap is prefix-based by design: 'templates/prompts/**/x.md' overlaps 'templates/prompts/y.md' although no file matches both. When a claim is refused for an overlap that cannot be real, narrow the claim's --globs to the literal paths (and widen later with ddflow update once the holder finishes) rather than waiting for or forcing past the holder.

**Why.** B-fix-bad-mentions: claim refused on prompts/**/research-companions.md vs prompts/mcp_instructions.md; claiming the literal commands/research-companions.md path succeeded, three of four fixes landed while the sibling held mcp_instructions.md

**Seen in:** B-fix-bad-mentions

## grep

### git grep -o undercounts with many -F patterns: re-match whole lines instead

**Rule.** To learn WHICH of many fixed-string patterns occur, run git grep without -o and re-match the returned lines in Python

**Why.** B17 research: git grep --cached -o -h -w -F with ~190 -e patterns reported agent_id 19 times while -c showed it in many files, so live identifiers looked deleted

**How to apply.** git grep -h -w -F -e ... (whole lines), then set(regex.findall(lines))

**Seen in:** B17

## guards

### A new module of helpers for later consumers needs [kept] entries in unreferenced_functions.toml

**Rule.** Every public helper with no production caller yet is listed under [kept] with the consumer task id, in the same change

**Why.** tests/test_architecture_guards.py ratchet unreferenced_functions has baseline 0; the selected unit_tests run failed on 5 new drift.py helpers

### A refactor that deletes a deferred import must lower that module's guard baseline in the same change

**Rule.** Run tests/test_architecture_guards.py when a change removes a function-level import or other counted pattern

**Why.** The ratchets fail when a count drops below its baseline ('now lower it'), so the ci gate fails on a clean refactor

**How to apply.** Edit tests/guard_baselines/<guard>/<module>.toml in the same commit and widen the item's globs to include it first

## help-first

### Read a subcommand's help before its flags when the verb was not used today

**Rule.** Any ddflow subcommand not run in this session yet: run  before passing flags not seen this session.

**How to apply.** hard blocker: ensuring guesses cost more than helps.

## hooks

### A hook's all-paths-are-mine guard fails whenever ddflow's own event shards are dirty

**Rule.** Never gate a derived-file commit on the whole working tree being clean: ddflow keeps uncommitted event shards in the primary; gate on what would be STAGED

**Why.** post-merge pins fold required every changed path to be a pin, so it never folded in the primary and README.md stayed dirty all night (B099544a590)

### A branch cut before a config knob cannot commit until it merges main: merge with --no-commit first

**Rule.** When a salvaged/stale worktree's commit hook dies with 'unknown knob' on the primary's .ddflow/config.toml, set the uncommitted work aside as a patch, run 'git merge main --no-commit', commit the merge, then re-apply and commit the work.

**Why.** The hook runs 'python -m ddflow', which puts the worktree's cwd first on sys.path, so the branch's OLD ddflow code reads the primary's NEWER config and refuses the unknown knob on every commit, including the salvage commit (B-precommit-companion, 2026-09-29; B9cb7dd1c3b fixed tolerance only for code containing the fix).

## identity

### Never keep your ddflow identity in a file another agent can rewrite: pass --agent on the command line itself

**Rule.** Spell --agent <id> (or DDFLOW_AGENT) inline on every ddflow call; do not rely on a wrapper script in a scratch directory.

**Why.** Subagents of one session share its scratchpad. On B-fix-trailer-names-item a wrapper 'dd' holding --agent fix-trailer-id was overwritten by the fix-staged-paths agent with its own id, and 138 events (claim, every gate, merge, complete, bug fixed) were recorded as fix-staged-paths, in that agent's shard.

**How to apply.** Before closing, grep the uncommitted shards for your item id; git status must show your own shard modified.

**Seen in:** B-fix-trailer-names-item

## ids

### With several agents on one queue, never file under the next free number: use a descriptive id (B-<slug>) and confirm it is unused

**Rule.** Before task add, pick an id derived from the work (B-add-refuses-dup-id), not max(B<n>)+1, and confirm it is free (ddflow show <id> must fail). Parallel agents each guess the same next number from their own view, and an add over an existing id overwrote that item's title/globs without warning, even a claimed one mid-pipeline (a duplicate id is now refused, but a numbered id still races). If a numbered id is required, re-read ddflow status immediately before adding.

**Why.** 2026-09-28: three agents each picked the next number within minutes (B205-B208 collided twice); four other agents' items were overwritten, one claimed and mid-pipeline, and one agent's lease and gate records ended up under another agent's title, where complete would have counted them.

**How to apply.** for id in ...; do ddflow show $id >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo TAKEN; done before filing. After a collision: void the stray gate records with a reason, release, re-file under a new id, remove the duplicates; restore a clobbered item by re-adding its prior task.added fields from the event log.

**Seen in:** B16042585f4, B6bd279367e

## import

### Check an import's dropped and held items against the project's own handoff/status document before trusting the queue

**Rule.** After ddflow import, compare every item the notes say was NOT imported or was held against the project's handoff: the importer's disposition heuristics dropped 38.9/38.10, P42.8 and held C11, the item the handoff says to start with

**Why.** Disposition rules measured on one project (run_nemo_run) misread another's conventions (home-simulator: '**ID** title' with prose after the id, '(not started)' sub-headings under SHIPPED sections)

**Seen in:** home-simulator cutover 2026-09-29; bugs B-imp-*

## intent

### When the operator changes a decision mid-task, rewrite the item's body the same moment

**Rule.** A cross-family review judges the diff against the item's title and body as its intent. If a decision changes after the item was filed (here: minor bump -> patch bump), update the body when the change is made, or every review reports the correct code as contradicting the spec -- four findings and a failed critic gate for a change that was right.

**Why.** B-release-every-push's body still said 'always bump the minor version' after the operator made CI patch-only; the critic review returned 2 HIGH, 1 MEDIUM, 1 LOW, all this mismatch.

**How to apply.** ddflow update <id> --body when the operator's instruction supersedes the filed one; quote both instructions and mark which supersedes.

## kilo

### The roborev daemon leaks a .kilo process per review, which saturates the shared LAN reviewer

**Rule.** Before and during long review work, reap orphaned '.kilo run' processes (ppid 1); run one review at a time per LAN endpoint

**Why.** 2026-09-29: the roborev daemon (roborev daemon run) spawns 'node kilo run' -> '.kilo run' per job; when the job ends the node launcher exits and the native .kilo child is re-parented to init and keeps querying the LAN endpoint. 18 were reaped at one point, 9 more an hour later; with them live every ddflow critic timed out at 3600 s or came back off-contract. Wrapping roborev in 'timeout' leaks the same way.

**How to apply.** for p in $(pgrep -f 'kilo run --format json'); do [ "$(ps -o ppid= -p $p | tr -d ' ')" = 1 ] && kill $p; done -- or restart the roborev daemon; the durable fix belongs in roborev/kilo (kill the process group).

**Seen in:** recovery session s20260929T151921-3202694

## lanes

### Never run a generically named script from a scratchpad lanes share: another lane's script runs under its identity

**Rule.** Lanes of one session share one scratchpad directory. Do not keep an executable there under a generic name and re-run it later: another lane can overwrite it, and you then act on that lane's item as that agent. Run commands inline, or name the file after the lane and read it back before each run. A refusal naming a pid, item or agent you do not recognise means stop and look at what you actually ran before suspecting the tool.

**Why.** sw-gitident's review.sh was overwritten by sw-pilottoy's at the same path. A re-run reviewed SW-pilot-toy under sw-pilottoy's name and used one of its review rounds. An earlier refusal naming the other lane's pid had been read as a possible ddflow defect, when it was correct.

**Seen in:** fix-B6a483bb0f5, SW-pilot-toy

## layering

### A change to ddflow/api/gates.py or services/gates/* must run test_layering, test_module_splits and test_gate_econ_tests before merge

**Rule.** Those files sit at an import cycle and a 600-line module limit.

**Why.** Three merges to the gates code broke main in one day (module size, an api<->api.gates cycle, a ruff import order).

**How to apply.** Add those three test files to the item's selected tests by hand when the diff touches the gates code.

**Seen in:** coordinator 2026-10-17

## leases

### A '**' glob conflicts with every live claim under its literal prefix: claim literal paths when a sibling holds a file in the same directory

**Rule.** globs_overlap is prefix-based by design: 'templates/prompts/**/x.md' overlaps 'templates/prompts/y.md' although no file matches both. When a claim is refused for an overlap that cannot be real, narrow the claim's --globs to the literal paths (and widen later with ddflow update once the holder finishes) rather than waiting for or forcing past the holder.

**Why.** B-fix-bad-mentions: claim refused on prompts/**/research-companions.md vs prompts/mcp_instructions.md; claiming the literal commands/research-companions.md path succeeded, three of four fixes landed while the sibling held mcp_instructions.md

**Seen in:** B-fix-bad-mentions

### Leases claimed for subagents expire during long work: the coordinator keeps them alive

**Rule.** When a coordinator claims items for subagents (ddflow --agent <name> claim), nobody heartbeats unless told to: a subagent's run plus its review round easily exceeds lease.ttl_s (30 min), the lease lapses, and ddflow next offers the item again while its author is still editing the worktree. Either instruct each subagent to heartbeat, or run one background loop that heartbeats every delegated lease while its item is running.

**Why.** 2026-09-29: B-fix-remedy-texts dropped out of ddflow next's running set mid-rework; noticed only because it appeared as 'blocked by the parallelism cap' instead of running.

**How to apply.** for each (item, agent): ddflow --agent <agent> heartbeat <item> every ~10 min while `ddflow show <item>` says running.

## lint

### Run ruff format (and ruff check) on the Python files you touched before every commit

**Rule.** Before committing or running the item's gates, run 'uv run ruff format <touched files>' and 'uv run ruff check <touched files>'; put pure formatting changes in their own commit. Agents must not leave formatting to the pre-push hook or to CI.

**Why.** On 2026-10-24..26 the CI Lint step and the pre-push stage failed repeatedly on 'ruff format --check' and 'ruff check' (an unused variable in a test, unformatted files after merges), found only at push time or by an unlucky agent's ci; each cost a red main, a bug, and an agent run. ruff format is deterministic and takes under a second.

**How to apply.** In a worktree: 'uv run ruff format <files> && uv run ruff check <files>' before 'git commit'; for a merge conflict resolution re-run it on the merged files; when fixing a Bci-ruff-* bug run 'uv run ruff format .' only on the failing files and commit it separately with a short message; 'ddflow precommit' runs the project's hooks if you want the exact CI set.

**Seen in:** Bci-ruff-format-check-ci-lint-71de8acaec-8d0f618, Bci-ruff-check-ci-lint-28f149cf83-12d29f5, B3943adc584

## lint-exempt

### ddflow --lint-exempt closes only CI-filed Bci-* bugs, not manually-filed ddflow bug found bugs

**Rule.**

## list

### `ddflow list` clamps --limit at 1000 with no paging: check `total` against `shown` before trusting a count

**Rule.** A report or script built on a silently truncated list undercounts.

**Why.** The queue has 2352 tasks; wave tables, a restamp of 24 new tasks and the first depth computation used 1000 of them and were wrong.

**How to apply.** Read the JSON `truncated`/`total` fields; page by --state and --tag until shown == total (DX-list-paging will fix the tool).

**Seen in:** coordinator 2026-10-17

## load

### A worker count fixed in a committed hook (-n auto) is per-core on the host that runs it

**Rule.** Substitute the computed count in the local runner (a temp copy of the hook config), keep the committed config for CI, and bound concurrent full runs host-wide

**Why.** B26b5951f2b: 2-3 CI-parity runs of 192 workers each gave load 337

### The load-per-core governor only acts in `parallel = auto`; a fixed cap bypasses it, and agent launches by hand bypass it too

**Rule.** The signals (load/cores, memory, disk) shrink the limit only when the limit is adaptive.

**Why.** Local config had parallel = fixed at 7 while two `pytest -n 48` full suites ran at once and load hit 119-160 on a 192-core host.

**How to apply.** Keep parallel = auto with load_per_core high = 0.80 and a raised max_parallel_max; take the offered count from `ddflow next` before launching agents; never run two full suites at once (DX-suite-host-lock).

**Seen in:** coordinator 2026-10-17

### Unexplained failure with no repro: ship diagnostics first, then fix what they show

**Rule.** When a check failed twice, passed on rerun and cannot be reproduced, do not guess a cause: first make the next failure explain itself (persist the failing step's table and each command's bounded stdout/stderr to a git-ignored file whose path is printed in the failure line), harden only what you can show misjudges, then run it repeatedly under load.

**Why.** B-dryrun-flake: the two failures of scripts/ci/upgrade-dry-run left nothing; 15 reruns passed, and the three suspected causes (clone racing git writes, live shards read mid-write, another agent's snapshot tag counted as ours) were real misjudgements in unit tests but are not what the first captured failure was. That one (1 in 15 loaded runs) was step 6: the MCP handshake did not propose the upgrade. The server's start check is bounded by [upgrade].start_timeout_s (10 s), the plan of this repository's 39k-event log takes 7-11 s, so under load it very probably timed out; the transcript cut the reply text (a command that exits 0 keeps few characters), so this is inferred, not read.

**How to apply.** Add the transcript before the fix; keep the reply a step judges (not only the exit code) in it; make load-dependent product bounds explicit in the rehearsal (give it time, and report a timeout as unavailable, never pass or fail). Close the bug only on 20 green loaded runs plus a clean week.

**Seen in:** B-dryrun-flake

## manifest

### A capped manifest must say what it dropped

**Rule.** Any list in a reviewer prompt that is capped (names, files) ends with 'and N more'; the manifest's own 4-name cap hid for_review and the reviewer called it missing

**Why.** rubber_duck on DX-review-manifest

## mcp

### A new top-level CLI command needs a covered-by declaration or tests/test_mcp_parity.py fails only in ci

**Rule.** When adding a CLI verb that rides an existing MCP tool as an action, also add Command(path=(verb,), reason=...) in surfaces/declared

**Why.** B-hx-cli: harness list/show/doctor passed the item's own tests and the 1837-test selection, and failed test_every_cli_command_is_reachable_over_mcp after a 16 minute whole-suite ci

**How to apply.** Run tests/test_mcp_parity.py tests/test_command_registry.py right after adding a parser

### A budget turned report-only must be relaxed in every enforcing site

**Rule.** When a hard limit becomes report-only (D-mcp-budget-report), grep every enforcer: upgrade_dryrun.tools_problems and test_kind_data_surface still hard-failed the 100,000 cap

### An api function behind an MCP tool's payload key must carry that key on every path, refusals included

**Rule.** When an api function's Outcome backs an MCP tool with `"payload": "<key>"`, build the projected data (including `<key>`, typically `rows`) BEFORE any validation, and pass it (`**data`) to every `O.refused`/`O.nothing` return as well as the success return. Never return a bare `O.refused(kind, reason)` from such a function. Verify it by calling the tool over MCP with an argument that triggers the refusal and asserting the reason survives -- a CLI test cannot catch this, because the CLI prints `out.reason` without projecting.

**Why.** In `mcp.py`, `_outcome_result` computes `out.body(payload_key)` before its refusal handling, and `Outcome.body(key)` is `self.data[key]`. So a refusal that omits the key raises KeyError, `serve` catches it, and the caller gets JSON-RPC -32603 "internal error: '<key>'" with the real remedy discarded. The CLI half is unaffected, so only an MCP-level test sees it.

**How to apply.** For any new/changed api function with a payload-keyed tool: (1) initialise the data dict with the key before validating; (2) grep the function for `O.refused(`/`O.nothing(` and confirm each passes `**data`; (3) add an MCP test that triggers each refusal and asserts a distinctive reason substring appears (not just a word that also appears in the JSON body).

**Seen in:** B196

## merge

### Every task adds its exemptions to the same line of constants-exemptions.toml, so merges conflict

**Rule.** Append new exempt entries at the END of the [exempt] table, never at its top

**Why.** three merges of main conflicted on the same insertion point

### A hook's all-paths-are-mine guard fails whenever ddflow's own event shards are dirty

**Rule.** Never gate a derived-file commit on the whole working tree being clean: ddflow keeps uncommitted event shards in the primary; gate on what would be STAGED

**Why.** post-merge pins fold required every changed path to be a pin, so it never folded in the primary and README.md stayed dirty all night (B099544a590)

### Check gate status before ddflow merge; chained commands skip the check

**Rule.** Run ddflow gate status and read every box before merge; never chain gate run, record, merge and complete in one command

**Why.** DX-agent-final-summary merged with ci and unit_tests unrecorded and left main red (B94d11818c1)

### Derived files dirtied in the primary checkout block every agent's merge: keep the primary clean

**Rule.** ddflow merge refuses a dirty primary tree.

**Why.** pins regenerate, upgrade --apply and a hook left .gitattributes, .ddflow/.gitignore and README.md edited; four agents lost time and one used --allow-dirty.

**How to apply.** Before launching agents run `git -C PRIMARY status --short`; revert or commit derived files through a chore claim; never --allow-dirty.

**Seen in:** coordinator 2026-10-17

### Close a bug found mid-task with 'bug fixed' BEFORE merging the item

**Rule.** Run ddflow bug fixed <id> --regression-test ... while the item's worktree still exists; after merge the worktree is gone and the regression check records could-not-run

**Why.** bug fixed verifies the regression test against the pre-fix source from the fix task's worktree; merge removes it (B4dd9658753, Bd5adf89e33 both closed could-not-run; both were verified by hand against main's code)

## monitor

### pgrep -f inside a wait loop matches the loop's own command line and never ends

**Rule.** Wait on a file or a pid, never on pgrep -f of a string the waiting command itself contains

**Why.** Three monitor loops 'until ! pgrep -f review B-hx-x' never finished; killing them also killed a shell

**How to apply.** until grep -q 'recorded ITEM.critic' FILE

## mutation

### Pick the tests for a mutation by file, not by covered line

**Rule.** When judging a mutant, run every test file that reaches the module, not only the tests whose coverage context touches the mutated line, and run the sample against a real git checkout (a git archive copy fails 8 repo-shape tests, a full-suite -x run then 'kills' everything).

**Why.** regexsafe.py mutants 'survived' the 7 tests whose contexts covered the line and were killed by the 85-test file set (2 of 3 re-checked mutants failed 1-2 tests); the git-archive copy had 8 baseline failures that made every -x run look like a kill.

**How to apply.** Baseline the exact test set on the unmutated tree first; a survivor is 'survived' only on the file-level set; equivalent mutants (default-arg constants, decorator lines, return '' vs None) are set aside by reading, not by running.

**Seen in:** U4

### A gate that checks a committed ref cannot be proved by a working-tree mutation

**Rule.** Before registering a mutation for a gate, check what the gate reads: gate verify edits the worktree uncommitted, so a gate that checks HEAD (ci) reports PASSED on mutated source and the proof is vacuous in the wrong direction.

**Why.** gate verify <item> ci ran 19.5 min / 1264 cpu-min and said ci cannot see the mutation; ci run merges the committed branch in a scratch tree (B-verify-ci-blind). A related trap: a test that asserts a registered mutation applies exactly once turns the gate red for EVERY mutation, because the suite runs with the mutation applied (the critic caught it).

**How to apply.** Register mutations only for gates that read the working tree (unit_tests). For a committed-ref gate, fix verify to commit the mutation first. Keep any test about the registry tolerant of the applied state.

**Seen in:** U4-mutation-registry

### Mutation-test a file from a saved copy, never undo the mutant with git checkout while the file has uncommitted edits

**Rule.** Before mutating a file to prove a test fails, commit the real edit or cp the file aside; restore with cp from that copy

**Why.** B-fix-registry-504: 'git checkout <file>' to drop a one-line mutant also discarded the uncommitted review fix in the same file; caught only because git diff --stat showed the file missing

**How to apply.** cp f /scratch/f.bak; sed mutant; run test; cp /scratch/f.bak f; git diff --stat

**Seen in:** B-fix-registry-504

## needs

### A task that needs a decide task is stuck for good once the decide task is abandoned as a decision

**Rule.** Do not put a decide task in another task's needs; the decision record governs by globs. If one is there, drop the edge with ddflow update --needs once the decision is recorded.

**Why.** ddflow treats an abandoned prerequisite as unsatisfied and the convention settles a decide task by abandoning it. 67 tasks waited forever on 2026-10-15 (9 on nothing else); the brief said 'X is abandoned' but nothing called it stuck.

**How to apply.** Before abandoning a decide task, list its dependents (ddflow show of the dependents, or the next output) and drop the edge; doctor will report such an edge once B9eeecd134c is fixed.

## onboarding

### Check an import's dropped and held items against the project's own handoff/status document before trusting the queue

**Rule.** After ddflow import, compare every item the notes say was NOT imported or was held against the project's handoff: the importer's disposition heuristics dropped 38.9/38.10, P42.8 and held C11, the item the handoff says to start with

**Why.** Disposition rules measured on one project (run_nemo_run) misread another's conventions (home-simulator: '**ID** title' with prose after the id, '(not started)' sub-headings under SHIPPED sections)

**Seen in:** home-simulator cutover 2026-09-29; bugs B-imp-*

### ddflow setup and import land in the PRIMARY checkout even when run from a linked worktree: onboard a project on its default branch, not on a feature branch

**Rule.** Run adopt/import/hooks for a project from its primary checkout on the default branch, and commit the result there with explicit paths

**Why.** repo_root() resolves --git-common-dir by design (one event log per repo); running adopt in a home-simulator worktree wrote AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .mcp.json and .ddflow/ into the primary checkout, leaving the worktree branch empty

**Seen in:** home-simulator cutover 2026-09-29

## outage

### Reviewer outage mid-loop: unavailable delta overwrites a passed round

**Rule.** when the LAN DeepSeek is down, do not start a delta round after a passed one

**Why.** fleet-r-gates 2026-10-19: delta round got connection refused and replaced fix-Be81c39acb8's passed rubber_duck/critic with unavailable; complete then refused (no reviewer ran); roborev kilo jobs hung 20+ min on the same outage (B277e2a224f)

**How to apply.** curl the reviewer /v1/models before any re-review; merge first (merge does not need reviewers), complete once it is back
